Notation and object dimensions for the common BTSBM interface

2026-10-16

Source: vignettes/Notation.Rmd
Notation.Rmd

Overview

All supported models use the same public workflow:

data <- as_bt_data(wins) # or as_rankings(rankings)
model <- bt_sbm_model()  # or another BT/PL model constructor
fit <- fit_model(data, model, mcmc_control())

The data object validates the observations, the model object states the likelihood and latent structure, and mcmc_control() contains computational settings. fit_model() always returns a btsbm_fit object. The lower-level gibbs_bt_*() functions remain available for compatibility, but new analyses should use this common architecture.

Data notation

Pairwise outcomes

For \(n\) items, let \(w_{ij}\) be the number of times item \(i\) defeats item \(j\). The directed win matrix is

\[ \mathbf W=(w_{ij})\in\mathbb N^{n\times n}, \qquad w_{ii}=0, \]

and the number of comparisons for an unordered pair is

\[ n_{ij}=w_{ij}+w_{ji}. \]

as_bt_data() stores these quantities as data$wins, data$n_items, and data$item_labels. Users do not supply \(\mathbf N\); it is computed when needed.

Ranking outcomes

For \(L\) observed rankings of length \(m\), row \(\ell\) of the integer matrix \(\boldsymbol\rho\) lists item identifiers from most to least preferred. A row may be a complete ranking or a top-\(m\) prefix from one common universe of \(n\) available items.

as_rankings() stores data$rankings with dimension L x m, together with data$n_rankings, data$rank_length, data$n_items, and stable item and ranking labels.

Model notation

The package separates the observation likelihood from the latent structure.

Constructor Likelihood Sampled partition Strength used by an observation
bt_model() Bradley–Terry none item strength \(\lambda_i\)
bt_sbm_model() Bradley–Terry item labels \(x_i\) block strength \(\lambda_{x_i}\)
pl_model() Plackett–Luce none item strength \(\lambda_i\)
pl_sbm_model() Plackett–Luce item labels \(x_i\) block strength \(\lambda_{x_i}\)
pl_mixture_model() Plackett–Luce ranking labels \(z_\ell\) profile-specific strength \(\lambda_{z_\ell i}\)
pl_lbm_model() Plackett–Luce \(x_i\) and \(z_\ell\) profile-by-item-block strength \(\lambda_{z_\ell x_i}\)

For Bradley–Terry models,

\[ \Pr(i\text{ defeats }j)=\frac{\lambda_i}{\lambda_i+\lambda_j}, \]

with \(\lambda_i\) replaced by \(\lambda_{x_i}\) in a BT–SBM. For a Plackett–Luce ranking, the probability of the item selected at each position is its positive strength divided by the total strength of the remaining risk set.

Prior and control objects

Positive strengths use latent_strength(shape, rate). Latent partitions use one of the following common constructors:

gnedin_prior(gnedin_hyperparameter = 0.5)
dirichlet_process_prior(concentration = 1)
pitman_yor_prior(concentration = 1, discount = 0.2)
finite_partition(max_clusters = 4, concentration = 1)

If iter is the total number of iterations and warmup is the discarded prefix, the number of saved draws is

\[ S=\texttt{iter}-\texttt{warmup}. \]

These names are shared by BT and PL models through mcmc_control(iter, warmup, seed, ...).

The btsbm_fit object

Every fit has the same top-level components:

fit$data
fit$model
fit$control
fit$draws
fit$diagnostics
fit$elapsed

The contents of fit$draws depend on the selected structure.

Draw component Meaning Dimension or form
item_cluster sampled \(x_i\) S x n integer matrix
ranking_cluster sampled \(z_\ell\) S x L integer matrix
n_item_clusters occupied item blocks length S
n_ranking_clusters occupied ranking profiles length S
latent_strength sampler-scale strengths matrix for simple models; list of length S for variable-dimensional models
item_strength item-level reported strengths S x n when defined
component_strength PL-mixture profile strengths list of length S
cell_strength PL–LBM profile-by-block strengths list of length S

Raw cluster numbers have no meaning across MCMC draws. Paper-style BT–SBM summaries relabel each draw by decreasing block strength, so cluster 1 is the strongest occupied block. Pairwise co-clustering summaries, such as posterior_similarity(), are label-invariant and do not require this step.

Posterior summaries and plots

The public summaries consume the btsbm_fit object directly:

posterior_strength(fit)
strength_summary(fit)
posterior_similarity(fit, target = "item")
log_lik(fit)
mcmc_diagnostics(fit)

For a BT–SBM, the paper-oriented outputs use the same fit object:

pretty_table_K_distribution(fit)
plot_block_adjacency(fit)
plot_assignment_probabilities(fit)
plot_rank_intervals(fit)

plot_assignment_probabilities() conditions on the posterior modal number of item blocks by default. Supply max_n_clust = K to condition on another sampled value. This separates uncertainty in item membership from uncertainty in the number of blocks.

Log-likelihood dimensions

log_lik(fit) returns one contribution per observational unit:

  • for BT models, an S x D matrix, where \(D\) is the number of observed unordered pairs \((i,j)\) with \(i<j\) and \(n_{ij}>0\);
  • for PL models, an S x L matrix, with one contribution per complete ranking row.

If loo is installed, loo_btsbm(fit) uses this same observation-level definition.

Minimal end-to-end example 

library(RBBayes)

pairwise <- tennis_toy(matches_per_pair = 8, seed = 1)
model <- bt_sbm_model(
  latent_strength = latent_strength(shape = 4, rate = exp(digamma(4))),
  item_clustering = gnedin_prior(gnedin_hyperparameter = 0.5)
)
fit <- fit_model(
  pairwise,
  model,
  mcmc_control(iter = 400, warmup = 200, seed = 2)
)

dim(fit$draws$item_cluster)       # S x n
length(fit$draws$n_item_clusters) # S
dim(log_lik(fit))                 # S x D

pretty_table_K_distribution(fit, p_min = 0)
plot_block_adjacency(fit)
plot_assignment_probabilities(fit)

Validation rules

  • Pairwise wins must form a square, finite, non-negative matrix with zero diagonal and unique item labels.
  • Ranking rows must contain distinct integer item identifiers in 1:item_count.
  • BT models require data from as_bt_data(); PL models require data from as_rankings().
  • warmup must be smaller than iter, and partition priors must satisfy their documented parameter constraints.

This interface keeps data preparation, model specification, computation, and posterior interpretation separate while using the same function architecture throughout the package.
